messages:
Zara: Quick follow-up from the all-hands pricing segment: two asks from PMs — (1) a 1-line explainer for why customers hit 429 despite having credits, and (2) a tiny billing example for fallback to cheaper models.

Ethan: 1-line explainer: "429 means you exceeded the account's request throughput (RPS/concurrency). Credits cover cost but do not raise rate caps; check X-RateLimit-* headers."

Priya: Billing example: if you requested model A (cost $0.0006/token) but we served model B fallback (cost $0.0002/token) for 1k tokens, billed amount = 1000 * $0.0002 = $0.20 (we bill actual served model). Credits applied after cost calc.

Zara: Helpful. Also add note that free-trial burst pool exists for first 48h and is finite.

billing-bot: Console -> Billing shows promo/credits and expiry (default 12 months). API: X-Credit-Balance header.

Ethan: Action: add the 1-line and example to FAQ and canned support replies today.

Zara: Thanks, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
